name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_AR_Q01 - Precipitation of silver chloride from cobalt ammonia complex

questiontext.text:
Assertion (A): One mole of \(\mathrm{CoCl_3 \cdot 5NH_3}\) precipitates two moles of \(\mathrm{AgCl}\) when treated with excess \(\mathrm{AgNO_3}\) solution in cold.

Reason (R): In \(\mathrm{[CoCl(NH_3)_5]Cl_2}\), two chloride ions satisfy primary valences as counter ions outside the coordination sphere and are ionisable, while one chloride ion satisfies both primary and secondary valences inside the coordination sphere.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
According to Werner's theory of coordination compounds, metals exhibit two types of linkages: ionisable primary valences satisfied by negative ions, and non-ionisable secondary valences (equal to the coordination number) satisfied by neutral molecules or negative ions within the coordination sphere.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Assertion Statement
In \(\mathrm{CoCl_3 \cdot 5NH_3}\), cobalt(III) has a secondary valence (coordination number) of \(6\). Five \(\mathrm{NH_3}\) molecules and one \(\mathrm{Cl^-}\) ion remain bound inside the coordination sphere, giving the formula \(\mathrm{[CoCl(NH_3)_5]^{2+}2Cl^-}\). In aqueous solution, it behaves as a \(1:2\) electrolyte, releasing \(2\text{ mol}\) of free \(\mathrm{Cl^-}\) ions per mole of complex. These \(2\text{ mol}\) of \(\mathrm{Cl^-}\) react with excess \(\mathrm{AgNO_3}\) in cold to precipitate \(2\text{ mol}\) of \(\mathrm{AgCl}\). Thus, the assertion statement is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Reason Statement
In \(\mathrm{[CoCl(NH_3)_5]Cl_2}\), the two chloride ions outside the square brackets act as counter ions satisfying only the ionisable primary valence, whereas the single chloride ion inside the square brackets is directly coordinated to \(\mathrm{Co^{3+}}\), satisfying both a primary valence (contributing to the \(+3\) oxidation state of cobalt) and a secondary valence (coordination number \(6\)). Thus, the reason statement is correct.

Step 4: Relationship and Final Conclusion
Because only the two ionisable counter-ion chloride ions outside the coordination sphere dissociate in water, one mole of the complex precipitates two moles of \(\mathrm{AgCl}\). Therefore, both statements are correct and the reason statement is the correct explanation of the assertion statement.

answer.text: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_AR_Q02 - Dissociation behaviour of double salts and complexes

questiontext.text:
Assertion (A): Mohr's salt, \(\mathrm{FeSO_4 \cdot (NH_4)_2SO_4 \cdot 6H_2O}\), dissociates completely into simple ions when dissolved in water, whereas potassium ferrocyanide, \(\mathrm{K_4[Fe(CN)_6]}\), does not dissociate into \(\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}\) and \(\mathrm{CN^-}\) ions.

Reason (R): Both double salts and coordination complexes are formed by the combination of two or more stable compounds in a stoichiometric ratio.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Addition compounds formed by combining two or more stable compounds in stoichiometric ratios are classified into double salts and coordination complexes based on their dissociation behaviour in aqueous solution.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Assertion Statement
Double salts such as Mohr's salt, \(\mathrm{FeSO_4 \cdot (NH_4)_2SO_4 \cdot 6H_2O}\), lose their identity in water by dissociating completely into simple ions (\(\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}\), \(\mathrm{NH_4^+}\), and \(\mathrm{SO_4^{2-}}\)). In contrast, a coordination compound such as \(\mathrm{K_4[Fe(CN)_6]}\) retains its complex ion \(\mathrm{[Fe(CN)_6]^{4-}}\) intact in solution and does not dissociate into \(\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}\) and \(\mathrm{CN^-}\) ions. Thus, the assertion statement is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Reason Statement
Both double salts and coordination complexes are indeed prepared by combining two or more stable compounds in a definite stoichiometric ratio. Thus, the reason statement is also correct.

Step 4: Relationship and Final Conclusion
The fact that both classes are formed in stoichiometric ratios does not explain why double salts dissociate completely into simple ions while complex ions remain intact in water; that difference arises from the strong coordinate bonding within the coordination sphere. Therefore, both statements are correct, but the reason statement is not the correct explanation of the assertion statement.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_AR_Q03 - Stability of chelate complexes and ambidentate ligands

questiontext.text:
Assertion (A): Complexes containing chelate ligands such as ethane-1,2-diamine (\(\mathrm{en}\)) tend to be more stable than similar complexes containing unidentate ligands.

Reason (R): An ambidentate ligand such as \(\mathrm{NO_2^-}\) binds simultaneously through both nitrogen and oxygen donor atoms to a single central metal ion to form a ring structure.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
A chelate ligand is a di- or polydentate ligand that uses two or more donor atoms simultaneously to bind a single central metal ion, forming a stable ring structure (chelate effect). An ambidentate ligand has two different donor atoms, either of which can coordinate to the metal ion at a time.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Assertion Statement
Ethane-1,2-diamine (\(\mathrm{H_2NCH_2CH_2NH_2}\)) is a didentate chelate ligand that coordinates through two nitrogen atoms simultaneously. Chelate complexes are thermodynamically more stable than similar complexes with unidentate ligands. Thus, the assertion statement is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Reason Statement
The nitrite ion (\(\mathrm{NO_2^-}\)) is an ambidentate ligand, meaning it can coordinate to a central metal ion either through its nitrogen atom (nitrito-N) or through one of its oxygen atoms (nitrito-O), but not simultaneously through both donor atoms to the same metal ion to form a chelate ring. Thus, the reason statement is incorrect.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Since the assertion statement is correct and the reason statement is incorrect, the conclusion is that the assertion holds true while the reason is false.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_AR_Q04 - Absence of geometrical isomerism in tetrahedral complexes

questiontext.text:
Assertion (A): Tetrahedral complexes of the type \(\mathrm{[MA_2B_2]}\) exhibit cis and trans geometrical isomerism.

Reason (R): In a tetrahedral complex, the relative positions of all four unidentate ligands attached to the central metal atom are identical with respect to one another.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Geometrical isomerism arises in heteroleptic complexes when ligands can occupy different spatial positions relative to one another (such as adjacent cis or opposite trans positions in square planar or octahedral complexes).

Step 2: Evaluation of the Assertion Statement
Geometrical isomerism is possible in square planar complexes of type \(\mathrm{[MX_2L_2]}\) and octahedral complexes, but it is not possible in tetrahedral complexes. Therefore, tetrahedral \(\mathrm{[MA_2B_2]}\) complexes do not exhibit cis and trans isomers. Thus, the assertion statement is incorrect.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Reason Statement
In a tetrahedral geometry, all four coordination sites are equidistant and adjacent to each other at the tetrahedral angle, so the relative positions of the unidentate ligands with respect to one another are identical. Thus, the reason statement is correct.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Since the assertion statement is incorrect and the reason statement is correct, the correct conclusion is that the assertion is false while the reason is true.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_AR_Q05 - Optical activity in octahedral platinum complexes

questiontext.text:
Assertion (A): In the coordination entity \(\mathrm{[PtCl_2(en)_2]^{2+}}\), only the cis-isomer shows optical activity, whereas the trans-isomer is optically inactive.

Reason (R): The cis-isomer of \(\mathrm{[PtCl_2(en)_2]^{2+}}\) lacks a plane of symmetry and forms non-superimposable mirror images (enantiomers), whereas the trans-isomer is symmetrical and superimposable on its mirror image.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Optical isomers (enantiomers) are chiral molecules or ions that form non-superimposable mirror images and rotate the plane of polarised light in opposite directions (dextro and laevo forms).

Step 2: Evaluation of the Assertion Statement
For an octahedral complex of the type \(\mathrm{[MCl_2(en)_2]^{n+}}\) such as \(\mathrm{[PtCl_2(en)_2]^{2+}}\), the cis-isomer exists as a pair of optically active enantiomers, whereas the trans-isomer does not exhibit optical activity. Thus, the assertion statement is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Reason Statement
In the cis-isomer, the two \(\mathrm{Cl^-}\) ligands are adjacent and the two bidentate \(\mathrm{en}\) ligands span adjacent edges in an arrangement that lacks any plane of symmetry, yielding non-superimposable mirror images. In the trans-isomer, the two \(\mathrm{Cl^-}\) ligands lie opposite each other and the two \(\mathrm{en}\) ligands lie in the equatorial plane, giving a plane of symmetry that makes its mirror image superimposable. Thus, the reason statement is correct.

Step 4: Relationship and Final Conclusion
Chirality (absence of symmetry and non-superimposable mirror images) is the exact criterion for optical activity. Therefore, both statements are correct and the reason statement is the correct explanation of the assertion statement.

questiontext.text:
Assertion (A): The complexes \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_5(SO_4)]Br}\) and \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_5Br]SO_4}\) are ionisation isomers that yield different ions in aqueous solution.

Reason (R): Solvate isomers such as \(\mathrm{[Cr(H_2O)_6]Cl_3}\) and \(\mathrm{[Cr(H_2O)_5Cl]Cl_2 \cdot H_2O}\) differ in whether a solvent molecule is directly bonded to the metal ion or present as free solvent molecules in the crystal lattice.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Structural isomers in coordination compounds have different chemical bonds. Ionisation isomerism occurs when a counter ion is itself a potential ligand and can exchange places with a ligand inside the coordination sphere. Solvate (or hydrate) isomerism occurs when solvent molecules differ in being coordinated to the metal ion versus being free in the crystal lattice.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Assertion Statement
In \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_5(SO_4)]Br}\), \(\mathrm{Br^-}\) is the counter ion (giving a precipitate of \(\mathrm{AgBr}\) with \(\mathrm{Ag^+}\)), whereas in \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_5Br]SO_4}\), \(\mathrm{SO_4^{2-}}\) is the counter ion (giving a precipitate of \(\mathrm{BaSO_4}\) with \(\mathrm{Ba^{2+}}\)). Hence, they are ionisation isomers yielding different ions in solution. Thus, the assertion statement is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Reason Statement
In \(\mathrm{[Cr(H_2O)_6]Cl_3}\) (violet) and \(\mathrm{[Cr(H_2O)_5Cl]Cl_2 \cdot H_2O}\) (grey-green), the difference lies in whether the \(\mathrm{H_2O}\) molecule is directly coordinated to \(\mathrm{Cr^{3+}}\) or present as water of crystallisation in the lattice. Thus, the reason statement is also correct.

Step 4: Relationship and Final Conclusion
Although both statements describe valid types of structural isomerism, the definition and example of solvate isomerism do not explain why \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_5(SO_4)]Br}\) and \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_5Br]SO_4}\) are ionisation isomers. Therefore, both statements are correct, but the reason statement is not the correct explanation of the assertion statement.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_AR_Q07 - Hybridisation and magnetic nature of cobalt octahedral complexes

questiontext.text:
Assertion (A): The octahedral complex \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}}\) is diamagnetic and is called an inner orbital complex, whereas \(\mathrm{[CoF_6]^{3-}}\) is paramagnetic and is called an outer orbital complex.

Reason (R): In \(\mathrm{[CoF_6]^{3-}}\), the \(\mathrm{Co^{3+}}\) ion undergoes \(d^2sp^3\) hybridisation using inner \(3d\) orbitals to accommodate six pairs of electrons from the six \(\mathrm{F^-}\) ligands.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
We are comparing two octahedral complexes of cobalt(III): \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}}\) and \(\mathrm{[CoF_6]^{3-}}\). The atomic number of cobalt is \(27\), so \(\mathrm{Co^{3+}}\) has a \(3d^6\) valence electron configuration.

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Under Valence Bond Theory (VBT), an octahedral complex forms either \(d^2sp^3\) hybrid orbitals (inner orbital or low spin complex, using \((n-1)d\) orbitals) or \(sp^3d^2\) hybrid orbitals (outer orbital or high spin complex, using \(nd\) orbitals).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
In a \(3d^6\) configuration, pairing of electrons into three \(3d\) orbitals leaves two \(3d\) orbitals vacant for \(d^2sp^3\) hybridisation and results in zero unpaired electrons (diamagnetic). Without pairing, the four unpaired electrons remain in \(3d\), requiring \(4s\), \(4p\), and two \(4d\) orbitals for \(sp^3d^2\) hybridisation (paramagnetic).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
In \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}}\), the six \(3d\) electrons pair up into three \(3d\) orbitals, leaving two \(3d\) orbitals vacant for \(d^2sp^3\) hybridisation; hence it is an inner orbital, diamagnetic complex. In \(\mathrm{[CoF_6]^{3-}}\), the \(3d\) electrons do not pair up, leaving four unpaired electrons in the \(3d\) subshell; therefore, \(\mathrm{Co^{3+}}\) uses outer \(4d\) orbitals to form \(sp^3d^2\) hybrid orbitals, making it an outer orbital, paramagnetic complex.

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The assertion statement correctly identifies \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}}\) as diamagnetic (inner orbital) and \(\mathrm{[CoF_6]^{3-}}\) as paramagnetic (outer orbital). The reason statement incorrectly claims that \(\mathrm{[CoF_6]^{3-}}\) uses \(d^2sp^3\) hybridisation with inner \(3d\) orbitals instead of \(sp^3d^2\) with outer \(4d\) orbitals. Thus, the assertion statement is correct and the reason statement is incorrect.

Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_AR_Q08 - Geometry and magnetism of four-coordinate nickel complexes

questiontext.text:
Assertion (A): Both \(\mathrm{[NiCl_4]^{2-}}\) and \(\mathrm{[Ni(CN)_4]^{2-}}\) have tetrahedral geometry and are paramagnetic with two unpaired electrons.

Reason (R): In \(\mathrm{[Ni(CN)_4]^{2-}}\), the \(\mathrm{Ni^{2+}}\) ion has a \(3d^8\) configuration and undergoes \(dsp^2\) hybridisation with all \(3d\) electrons paired, whereas in \(\mathrm{[NiCl_4]^{2-}}\), \(\mathrm{Ni^{2+}}\) undergoes \(sp^3\) hybridisation leaving two unpaired electrons.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Both \(\mathrm{[NiCl_4]^{2-}}\) and \(\mathrm{[Ni(CN)_4]^{2-}}\) are four-coordinate complexes containing \(\mathrm{Ni^{2+}}\) (oxidation state \(+2\)), which has a \(3d^8\) electronic configuration.

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
In Valence Bond Theory, a coordination number of \(4\) corresponds to \(sp^3\) hybridisation (tetrahedral geometry) or \(dsp^2\) hybridisation (square planar geometry).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
For a \(3d^8\) ion, \(dsp^2\) hybridisation requires one vacant \(3d\) orbital, which is obtained by pairing the two unpaired \(3d\) electrons into one orbital. In \(sp^3\) hybridisation, only \(4s\) and \(4p\) orbitals are used, leaving the \(3d^8\) electrons unpaired according to Hund's rule.

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
In \(\mathrm{[NiCl_4]^{2-}}\), \(\mathrm{Cl^-}\) does not cause pairing of the \(3d\) electrons; \(\mathrm{Ni^{2+}}\) undergoes \(sp^3\) hybridisation, resulting in tetrahedral geometry with two unpaired electrons (paramagnetic). In \(\mathrm{[Ni(CN)_4]^{2-}}\), the \(3d\) electrons pair up to vacate one \(3d\) orbital, allowing \(dsp^2\) hybridisation, which gives a square planar geometry with zero unpaired electrons (diamagnetic).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The assertion statement is incorrect because \(\mathrm{[Ni(CN)_4]^{2-}}\) is square planar and diamagnetic, not tetrahedral and paramagnetic. The reason statement accurately describes the hybridisation and electron pairing in both complexes. Therefore, the assertion statement is incorrect and the reason statement is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_AR_Q09 - Absence of low spin tetrahedral complexes in CFT

questiontext.text:
Assertion (A): Tetrahedral coordination entities rarely exhibit low spin electronic configurations.

Reason (R): For the same metal, ligands, and metal-ligand distances, the tetrahedral crystal field splitting energy \(\Delta_t\) is equal to \(\frac{4}{9}\Delta_o\), which is not sufficiently large to overcome the electron pairing energy \(P\).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In Crystal Field Theory (CFT), the choice between high spin and low spin electron distribution depends on the relative magnitudes of the crystal field splitting energy (\(\Delta\)) and the pairing energy (\(P\)). Low spin configurations occur only when \(\Delta > P\).

Step 2: Evaluation of the Assertion Statement
Experimentally and theoretically under CFT, tetrahedral complexes almost always adopt high spin configurations and rarely show low spin configurations. Thus, the assertion statement is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Reason Statement
For the same metal, same ligands, and identical metal-ligand distances, the tetrahedral splitting energy is less than half of the octahedral splitting energy, specifically \(\Delta_t = \frac{4}{9}\Delta_o\). Because \(\Delta_t\) is small, \(\Delta_t < P\) holds in almost all cases, so electrons preferentially occupy the higher \(t_2\) orbitals singly before pairing in the lower \(e\) orbitals. Thus, the reason statement is correct.

Step 4: Relationship and Final Conclusion
The small magnitude of \(\Delta_t = \frac{4}{9}\Delta_o\) relative to \(P\) directly prevents forced electron pairing in tetrahedral complexes. Therefore, both statements are correct and the reason statement is the correct explanation of the assertion statement.

Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_AR_Q10 - Origin of colour and crystal field splitting in titanium complex

questiontext.text:
Assertion (A): An aqueous solution of \(\mathrm{[Ti(H_2O)_6]^{3+}}\) appears violet in colour due to \(d\text{--}d\) electronic transition from the \(t_{2g}\) level to the \(e_g\) level, whereas heating \(\mathrm{[Ti(H_2O)_6]Cl_3}\) to remove water renders it colourless.

Reason (R): In an octahedral crystal field, the \(d_{x^2-y^2}\) and \(d_{z^2}\) orbitals are raised in energy by \(\frac{3}{5}\Delta_o\) and the \(d_{xy}\), \(d_{yz}\), and \(d_{xz}\) orbitals are lowered in energy by \(\frac{2}{5}\Delta_o\) relative to the average energy in a spherical crystal field.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In Crystal Field Theory, the colour of transition metal complexes arises from \(d\text{--}d\) transitions between split \(d\) orbital energy levels, where the observed colour is complementary to the wavelength of visible light absorbed.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Assertion Statement
In \(\mathrm{[Ti(H_2O)_6]^{3+}}\), \(\mathrm{Ti^{3+}}\) is a \(3d^1\) system with the single electron in the \(t_{2g}\) level. Absorption of blue-green light (\(498\text{ nm}\)) excites the electron to the \(e_g\) level (\(t_{2g}^1 e_g^0 \to t_{2g}^0 e_g^1\)), causing the complex to appear violet. When water ligands are removed by heating \(\mathrm{[Ti(H_2O)_6]Cl_3}\), crystal field splitting no longer occurs, so \(d\text{--}d\) transitions cannot take place and the substance becomes colourless. Thus, the assertion statement is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Reason Statement
In an octahedral field, the two \(e_g\) orbitals (\(d_{x^2-y^2}\) and \(d_{z^2}\)) point directly towards the ligands and increase in energy by \(\frac{3}{5}\Delta_o\), while the three \(t_{2g}\) orbitals (\(d_{xy}, d_{yz}, d_{xz}\)) lie between the axes and decrease in energy by \(\frac{2}{5}\Delta_o\) relative to the barycentre. Thus, the reason statement is also correct.

Step 4: Relationship and Final Conclusion
While the reason statement correctly gives the quantitative energy splitting of \(e_g\) and \(t_{2g}\) orbitals in an octahedral field, it does not explain why removing water ligands makes \(\mathrm{[Ti(H_2O)_6]Cl_3}\) colourless or why specifically blue-green light is absorbed to produce a violet colour. Therefore, both statements are correct, but the reason statement is not the correct explanation of the assertion statement.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_AR_Q11 - Synergic bonding in homoleptic metal carbonyls

questiontext.text:
Assertion (A): The metal-carbon bond in metal carbonyls such as \(\mathrm{[Ni(CO)_4]}\) and \(\mathrm{[Cr(CO)_6]}\) possesses both \(\sigma\) and \(\pi\) character, resulting in a synergic effect that strengthens the bond between \(\mathrm{CO}\) and the metal.

Reason (R): The \(\mathrm{M\text{--}C}\) \(\pi\) bond is formed by the donation of a lone pair of electrons from the carbonyl carbon into a vacant orbital of the metal, whereas the \(\mathrm{M\text{--}C}\) \(\sigma\) bond is formed by the donation of a pair of electrons from a filled \(d\) orbital of the metal into the vacant antibonding \(\pi^*\) orbital of carbon monoxide.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Homoleptic metal carbonyls exhibit synergic bonding in which ligand-to-metal \(\sigma\) donation and metal-to-ligand \(\pi\) back-donation mutually reinforce each other.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Assertion Statement
In metal carbonyls such as \(\mathrm{[Ni(CO)_4]}\) and \(\mathrm{[Cr(CO)_6]}\), the metal-carbon bond has both \(\sigma\) and \(\pi\) character. This dual interaction creates a synergic effect that strengthens the \(\mathrm{M\text{--}CO}\) bond. Thus, the assertion statement is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Reason Statement
The \(\mathrm{M\text{--}C}\) \(\sigma\) bond is actually formed by the donation of a lone pair of electrons from the carbonyl carbon into a vacant orbital of the metal, whereas the \(\mathrm{M\text{--}C}\) \(\pi\) bond is formed by the donation of a pair of electrons from a filled \(d\) orbital of the metal into the vacant antibonding \(\pi^*\) orbital of \(\mathrm{CO}\). The reason statement reverses the roles of the \(\sigma\) and \(\pi\) bonds and is therefore incorrect.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Since the assertion statement is correct and the reason statement is incorrect, the conclusion is that the assertion is true while the reason is false.
